coverage.assessment: The army-impulse chain, the copying of affidavits, and the cause and effect of the Butler quarrel survive. Three setups were thinned or lost. The 'worst liars were the candid' paradox lost its premise (F1). The 'attitude of prayer' sentence lacks its homage setup (F4). Moran is never introduced, although chapter 012 opens on his promotion (F7).

Lady Palmerston is introduced before Oliphant is said to have been met at her house. Thackeray's 1863 death is framed retrospectively. Hugo is placed at Geneva ten years afterwards. The candle-lit stair scene, the bedroom monologue, and 'the three young men' all resolve clearly.

The Minister's curt 'Palmerston wants a quarrel!', the footman's escalating mis-announcements, the Cabinet Minister's 'licking', Stirling's verdict, and Milnes's Hugo anecdote all keep correct speakers and rhythm.

The revision keeps 'Perhaps he was right... afterwards he felt less sure', 'at least, not then', 'Possibly', and 'perhaps exist still'. The Butler quarrel's attribution to Russell remains the Minister's belief.
The 1862 rage and the later retrospect stay distinct. No later apology to Palmerston or archival vindication is anticipated. The puzzle closes on an unresolved question.

Periodic sentences and the self-deflating terms 'small fry' and 'worm' survive. Several distinctive series and jokes were cut: the 'exasperated, furious, bitter' series (F2) and the coin-unearthing self-mockery (F3).

The foes-versus-friends inversion and the 'one could only receive' gulf hold. The Swinburne arc is thinned: his own ballads, the Atalanta penance, and the dispersal of Oliphant and Stirling are gone (F5). The Hugo test has also lost its stated reason (F6).
The Milnes dependency and the Palmerston-puzzle dependency are intact at both endpoints. For the Swinburne gulf, the local endpoint is intact, but chapter 023's revision removed the Swinburne recall.

strengths: The footman sequence keeps the full Handrew–Hanthony–Halexander escalation, so V4 lands with its setup.
Palmerston's wooden 'Ha! ... Ha! ... Ha!' and 'Yes! ... Yes! ... Yes!' keep their slow rhythm before 'a laugh of 1810'.
The Butler quarrel keeps the Minister's belief, the son's later doubt ('afterwards he felt less sure'), and the closing either/or question unresolved.
The Thackeray episode keeps the retrospective 'last time' framing, the 1863 date, and the dash rhythm of V3.
The revision restored 'as an American private secretary' in the Milnes–Hugo comparison, keeping the parallel between Milnes's helplessness and Adams's.
summary: The revision keeps the chapter's architecture, all eight verbatim anchors, both continuity-sensitive chronologies, and the open Palmerston puzzle. The editorial issues come from small revision-stage cuts. These remove setup for the diplomats' paradox about lying, the tear-choked emotional series behind 'If one shed tears', Milnes's coin-unearthing joke, and the 'ear' explanation of the Hugo test. One residue from the first draft remains: the 'attitude of prayer' sentence has no homage clause before it. The Swinburne partner endpoint was cut in chapter 023's revision.
